sources.content_summary: Stable publication depends on loader-correct tarballs, explicit monorepo version policy, OIDC publication, provenance, and a non-latest rehearsal.
key_points: Test packed tarballs through import, require, and TypeScript consumers.
Trusted publishing has explicit runner, Node, npm, and permission requirements.
Fixed and linked Changesets policies produce different release behavior.
An RC rehearsal must not mutate the stable dist-tag.
misconceptions: A source build proves the npm package works.
Publishing to latest is an acceptable release rehearsal.
Fixed and linked package groups are interchangeable.

sources.content_summary: React/Next, A2UI/A2A, Flutter/Riverpod, and Tauri each have ownership and maturity boundaries that the examples must expose rather than hide.
key_points: Next server requests require isolated graph instances and serializable hydration data.
A2UI v0.9.1 is the stable protocol target; action authorization remains application-owned.
Flutter genui remains experimental even when protocol fixtures pass.
Tauri shared-code certification is not equivalent to signed store distribution.
misconceptions: Official A2UI rendering authorizes entity mutations.
A working genui demo makes genui a stable dependency.
A Tauri desktop build proves mobile store readiness.
A process-global graph is safe for concurrent Next.js requests.

sources.content_summary: BDD, deterministic visual evidence, and branded documentation form one traceable proof product tied to an immutable candidate SHA.
key_points: Each stable claim maps from specification to Gherkin to executable result and evidence.
Visual baselines require a pinned rendering environment.
Traces diagnose behavior; video and screenshots are review receipts, not assertions.
GitHub Pages deployment should use a least-privilege artifact workflow.
misconceptions: Retrying a flaky BDD scenario until green is certification.
A logo on the default Docusaurus theme constitutes complete branding.
